text:
maria: Quick sync 45-- ran a set of weight-only INT8 bring-up runs for fenrir13b (main branch) comparing bitsandbytes (bnb-int8) vs our llm.int8 path. Posting bench + quality notes. Short summary: bnb gives slightly better p50 and peak tokens/sec on short requests; llmint8 is more faithful on long-context summarization and has fewer factual errors. Opinions on rollout?

devon: Dropping the raw nightly harness numbers (single A100-80GB, seq=512 for short tests and seq=2048 for long summaries, beam=1, streaming). Memory includes cache+activs.
```
Variant                 | tokens/sec (512) | p50 latency (ms) | tokens/sec (2048) | RougeL delta vs fp16
fp16 baseline           | 61.7             | 16.2             | 43.5              | 0.0
fenrir13b-bnb-wonly     | 84.3             | 12.0             | 57.8              | -2.7
fenrir13b-llmint8       | 78.1             | 13.2             | 60.2              | -1.0
```
Notes: bnb shows bigger wins at short seq; llmint8 actually slightly faster for long sequences in tokens/sec in this run (likely due to better KV/cache layout). RougeL measured on our longform summarization slice.

aj: Which bitsandbytes release and flags?

devon: bnb 0.41.6 with weight_only+fused-gemm kernels. llmint8 build from commit b3f4e9c (our per-channel scale + small outlier correction patch). No activation quantization in either.

sam: Human spot-checks on the long-summary slice (n=200): bnb produced more hallucinated "agenda" sections and invented action items ~14% of samples; llmint8 ~6%. Embedding similarity vs ref (our in-house embed model): bnb mean 0.84, llmint8 0.88, fp16 0.90.

maria: Do we have deterministic examples to show customers/product?

devon: Yup, example where bnb invents items:
```
Input: "Summarize meeting notes and list follow-ups."
Reference: 5 bullets (action items clearly enumerated)
bnb-wonly: generates 7 bullets, 2 are fabricated ("schedule infra sync weekly"), asserts owners.
llmint8: sticks to 5 bullets, adds a clarifying Q for missing owner on item 3.
```
Also observed numeric rounding differences in tables: bnb tends to produce rounded percentages where fp16 had exact integers; llmint8 preserved integers more often.

aj: Any perf failure modes? tail latency, out-of-memory?

devon: No OOMs on A100-80GB. Tail latency under concurrent load: bnb has worse p95 under high concurrency for large seq (we measured p95 spike ~2.1x baseline), llmint8 maintained p95 within 1.4x. Hypothesis: bnb fused kernels cause less predictable CUDA stream contention when many inflight requests.

sam: Deployment implications: bnb is attractive as an opt-in high-throughput mode for short completions. For long-form summarization and multi-turn chat we should prefer llmint8 by default to avoid factual regressions.

runtime-bot: Canary started fenrir13b-llmint8 on ded-gpu-pool at 2864012000. Canary size=6 instances, traffic=1%.

maria: Proposed rollout plan: default llmint8 for longform and chat routes; offer bnb-based "high-throughput" opt-in toggle for short completion routes. Add automatic fallback to fp16 when live eval RougeL drop > 2.0 or factual-error rate jumps > 10% relative to baseline.

aj: Canary policy suggestion: 2% traffic for 24h with live-eval hooks for longform slices, and immediate rollback on any error-rate spike (>3x) or latency SLO breach.

devon: I'll prepare rollout config + postdeploy live-eval job sampling 300 longform requests/hour and 100 short completions/hour. Will tag runs with exact binaries and commit hashes and upload artifacts.

maria: Action items:
- devon: push rollout config, include artifact links + bnb/llmint8 version details (ETA EOD)
- sam: add tailored p95/p99 alerts and memory thresholds for both variants (ETA +1 day)
- aj: draft customer comms describing the two-mode option and recommended defaults (ETA 48h)

devon: Artifacts will include: bench logs, embed sim CSV, human-eval spreadsheet. Will attach link in PR (s3://redwood-internal/bench/fenrir13b/2864-runset).

maria: Thanks. Small note: let's also add a small automated eval slice that checks "added action items" hallucination count per hour; useful signal for on-call.

sam: Good call.

maria: OK closing. Ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:
